topics: Circle equations in standard & general forms
Chord theorems & power of a point

body.en: Circles and conic sections comprise approximately 10% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Candidates must fluently convert circle equations between general and standard center-radius forms via completing the square, formulate tangent lines perpendicular to radial segments, apply circle power theorems (tangent-secant, intersecting chords), and analyze conic sections (ellipses and hyperbolas) by identifying their centers, vertices, axes, and foci.
body.ar: Circles and conic sections comprise approximately 10% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Candidates must fluently convert الدائرة المعادلات between general and standard center-نصف القطر forms via completing the square, formulate tangent lines perpendicular to radial segments, apply الدائرة power theorems (tangent-secant, intersecting chords), and analyze conic sections (ellipses and hyperbolas) by identifying their centers, vertices, axes, and foci.

label.en: Definition 6.1 — Circles, Tangents, and Conic Standard Forms
label.ar: تعريف 6.1 — Circles, Tangents, and Conic Standard Forms

body.en:
Fundamental definitions and algebraic models of circles and conics:
  • Circle Center-Radius Form:
    \[ (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 \]
    where \((h, k)\) is the center and \(r > 0\) is the radius.
  • Tangent Line Perpendicularity: A line tangent to a circle at point \(P(x_1, y_1)\) is strictly perpendicular to the radial segment connecting center \((h, k)\) to \(P\):
    \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{y_1 - k}{x_1 - h} \implies m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{radius}}} = -\frac{x_1 - h}{y_1 - k} \]
  • Standard Form of an Ellipse: Centered at \((h, k)\) with semi-major axis \(a\) and semi-minor axis \(b\) (\(a > b\)):
    \[ \frac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1 \quad (\text{horizontal major axis}) \]
    Focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\), with foci at \((h \pm c, k)\). Eccentricity is \(e = \frac{c}{a} < 1\).
  • Standard Form of a Hyperbola: Centered at \((h, k)\) with transverse axis along \(x\):
    \[ \frac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1 \]
    Focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\), with foci at \((h \pm c, k)\). Asymptotes are \(y - k = \pm \frac{b}{a}(x - h)\).
body.ar:
Fundamental definitions and algebraic models of circles and conics:
  • Circle Center-نصف القطر Form:
    \[ (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 \]
    where \((h, k)\) is the center and \(r > 0\) is the نصف القطر.
  • Tangent Line Perpendicularity: A line tangent to a الدائرة at point \(P(x_1, y_1)\) is strictly perpendicular to the radial segment connecting center \((h, k)\) to \(P\):
    \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{y_1 - k}{x_1 - h} \implies m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{m_{\text{radius}}} = -\frac{x_1 - h}{y_1 - k} \]
  • Standard Form of an القطع الناقص: Centered at \((h, k)\) with semi-major axis \(a\) and semi-minor axis \(b\) (\(a > b\)):
    \[ \frac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} + \frac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1 \quad (\text{horizontal major axis}) \]
    Focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\), with foci at \((h \pm c, k)\). Eccentricity is \(e = \frac{c}{a} < 1\).
  • Standard Form of a القطع الزائد: Centered at \((h, k)\) with transverse axis along \(x\):
    \[ \frac{(x - h)^2}{a^2} - \frac{(y - k)^2}{b^2} = 1 \]
    Focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\), with foci at \((h \pm c, k)\). خطوط التقارب are \(y - k = \pm \frac{b}{a}(x - h)\).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Circles & Conic Sections
label.ar: ● الحدس المفاهيمي العميق — Circles & Conic Sections

body.en: Euclidean Invariants, Locus Equations & Scaling Laws: In analytic geometry, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A circle of center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a tangent line at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the radius \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).
body.ar: Euclidean Invariants, Locus المعادلات & Scaling Laws: In analytic الهندسة, geometric loci translate into algebraic constraints via Euclidean distance \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}\). A الدائرة of center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\) satisfies \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), and a خط المماس at point \(P\) is strictly perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(CP\) (\(m_{\text{tan}} \cdot m_{\text{rad}} = -1\)). Under a similarity scale factor \(k\), all linear lengths scale by \(k\), surface areas scale by \(k^2\), and volumes scale by \(k^3\).

label.en: Theorem 6.1 — Power of a Point, Inscribed Angles, and Conic Discriminant
label.ar: مبرهنة 6.1 — Power of a Point, Inscribed Angles, and Conic Discriminant

body.en:
Analytical circle theorems and general quadratic conic classification:
  • Power of a Point Theorems: For an external point \(P\):
    1. Tangent-Secant Theorem: If \(PT\) is tangent at \(T\) and \(PAB\) is a secant line: \(PT^2 = PA \cdot PB\).
    2. Intersecting Chords Theorem: If chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at interior point \(M\): \(MA \cdot MB = MC \cdot MD\).
  • Inscribed Angle & Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorems:
    1. An inscribed angle is half the central angle subtending the same arc: \(\angle_{\text{inscribed}} = \frac{1}{2}\angle_{\text{central}}\).
    2. Opposite angles of any cyclic quadrilateral (inscribed in a circle) are supplementary: \(\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ\).
  • General Conic Classification (\(Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\)):
    Using the conic discriminant \(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC\) (for unrotated conics, \(B = 0\)):
    1. If \(B^2 - 4AC < 0\): Ellipse (or Circle if \(A = C\) and \(B = 0\)).
    2. If \(B^2 - 4AC = 0\): Parabola.
    3. If \(B^2 - 4AC > 0\): Hyperbola.
body.ar:
Analytical الدائرة theorems and general quadratic conic classification:
  • Power of a Point Theorems: For an external point \(P\):
    1. Tangent-Secant مبرهنة: If \(PT\) is tangent at \(T\) and \(PAB\) is a secant line: \(PT^2 = PA \cdot PB\).
    2. Intersecting Chords مبرهنة: If chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect at interior point \(M\): \(MA \cdot MB = MC \cdot MD\).
  • Inscribed الزاوية & Cyclic Quadrilateral Theorems:
    1. An inscribed الزاوية is half the central الزاوية subtending the same arc: \(\angle_{\text{inscribed}} = \frac{1}{2}\angle_{\text{central}}\).
    2. Opposite angles of any cyclic quadrilateral (inscribed in a الدائرة) are supplementary: \(\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ\).
  • General Conic Classification (\(Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\)):
    Using the conic discriminant \(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC\) (for unrotated conics, \(B = 0\)):
    1. If \(B^2 - 4AC < 0\): Ellipse (or Circle if \(A = C\) and \(B = 0\)).
    2. If \(B^2 - 4AC = 0\): Parabola.
    3. If \(B^2 - 4AC > 0\): Hyperbola.

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Circles & Conic Sections
label.ar: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Circles & Conic Sections (الدوائر والقطوع المخروطية)

body.en:
• Completing the Square for Circles: When converting general form \(x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\) to standard form \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), remember to add \((D/2)^2\) and \((E/2)^2\) to both sides of the equation. Forgetting to add them to the right-hand side produces an incorrect radius.
  • Tangent Perpendicularity: A line tangent to a circle at point \(P(x_1, y_1)\) is always perpendicular to the radius \(OP\). If the radius has slope \(m\), the tangent line has slope \(-1/m\).
  • Conic Identification from General Quadratic: In \(Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\): if \(A = C\), it is a circle; if \(A \neq C\) but both have the same sign (\(AC > 0\)), it is an ellipse; if \(A\) and \(C\) have opposite signs (\(AC < 0\)), it is a hyperbola; if either \(A = 0\) or \(C = 0\) (but not both), it is a parabola.
  • Focal Distance Formulas: For an ellipse, \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) (foci are inside the ellipse, so \(c < a\)). For a hyperbola, \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) (foci are outside the vertices, so \(c > a\)). Do not confuse these two relations!
body.ar:
• Completing the Square for Circles: عندما converting general form \(x^2 + y^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\) to standard form \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), remember to add \((D/2)^2\) and \((E/2)^2\) to both sides of the المعادلة. Forgetting to add them to the right-hand side produces an incorrect نصف القطر.
  • Tangent Perpendicularity: A line tangent to a الدائرة at point \(P(x_1, y_1)\) is always perpendicular to the نصف القطر \(OP\). If the نصف القطر has الميل \(m\), the خط المماس has الميل \(-1/m\).
  • Conic Identification from General Quadratic: In \(Ax^2 + Cy^2 + Dx + Ey + F = 0\): if \(A = C\), it is a الدائرة; if \(A \neq C\) but both have the same sign (\(AC > 0\)), it is an القطع الناقص; if \(A\) and \(C\) have opposite signs (\(AC < 0\)), it is a القطع الزائد; if either \(A = 0\) or \(C = 0\) (but not both), it is a القطع المكافئ.
  • Focal Distance الصيغ: For an القطع الناقص, \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) (foci are inside the القطع الناقص, so \(c < a\)). For a القطع الزائد, \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) (foci are outside the vertices, so \(c > a\)). Do not confuse these two relations!

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Circles & Conic Sections)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Circles & Conic Sections)

body.en:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central Angle & Circle Completion Works: Given \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the radius is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any circle, drawing diameter \(POQ\) splits an inscribed angle \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior angle theorem, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).
body.ar:
Why Inscribed Angles Equal Half the Central الزاوية & الدائرة Completion Works: المعطيات \(x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), completing the square in \(x\) and \(y\) simultaneously yields:

\[ (x + g)^2 - g^2 + (y + f)^2 - f^2 + c = 0 \implies (x + g)^2 + (y + f)^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c \]

Thus the center is \((-g, -f)\) and the نصف القطر is \(r = \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}\) (requiring \(g^2 + f^2 > c\)). In any الدائرة, drawing القطر \(POQ\) splits an inscribed الزاوية \(\angle APB\) into two isosceles triangles \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\) (since \(OA = OB = OP = r\)); by the exterior الزاوية المبرهنة, \(\angle AOB = 2\angle APB\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.A — General to Standard Circle Form & Tangent Equation
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.A — General to Standard الدائرة Form & Tangent المعادلة

body.en:
A circle is defined by \(x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y = 0\).
(a) Find the center \((h, k)\) and radius \(r\).
(b) Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle at the origin \((0, 0)\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Complete the square:
    \[ (x^2 - 6x + 9) + (y^2 + 8y + 16) = 0 + 9 + 16 \implies (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 25 \]
    Center: \(\mathbf{(3, -4)}\)
    Radius: \(r = \sqrt{25} = \mathbf{5}\)
  2. (b) Determine the tangent line at \((0, 0)\):
    Slope of the radial segment connecting center \((3, -4)\) to \((0, 0)\):
    \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{0 - (-4)}{0 - 3} = -\frac{4}{3} \]
    The tangent line is perpendicular, so its slope is the negative reciprocal:
    \[ m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{-4/3} = \frac{3}{4} \]
    Since the line passes through the origin \((0, 0)\), its equation is:
    \[ y = \frac{3}{4}x \implies \mathbf{3x - 4y = 0} \]
body.ar:
A الدائرة is defined by \(x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y = 0\).
(a) أوجد center \((h, k)\) and نصف القطر \(r\).
(b) أوجد معادلة the خط المماس to the الدائرة at the origin \((0, 0)\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Complete the square:
    \[ (x^2 - 6x + 9) + (y^2 + 8y + 16) = 0 + 9 + 16 \implies (x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 25 \]
    Center: \(\mathbf{(3, -4)}\)
    Radius: \(r = \sqrt{25} = \mathbf{5}\)
  2. (b) حدّد خط المماس at \((0, 0)\):
    Slope of the radial segment connecting center \((3, -4)\) to \((0, 0)\):
    \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{0 - (-4)}{0 - 3} = -\frac{4}{3} \]
    The خط المماس is perpendicular, so its الميل is the negative reciprocal:
    \[ m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{-4/3} = \frac{3}{4} \]
    Since the line passes through the origin \((0, 0)\), its المعادلة is:
    \[ y = \frac{3}{4}x \implies \mathbf{3x - 4y = 0} \]

label.en: Worked Example 6.B — Power of a Point & Tangent Segment Lengths
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.B — Power of a Point & Tangent Segment Lengths

body.en:
A point \(P\) is located at distance \(13\text{ cm}\) from the center \(O\) of a circle with radius \(5\text{ cm}\). A tangent line from \(P\) touches the circle at point \(T\).
(a) Find the length of the tangent segment \(PT\).
(b) A secant line through \(P\) intersects the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(PA = 8\text{ cm}\). Find the length of chord \(AB\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Tangent Segment Length:
    Radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to tangent \(PT\), forming right triangle \(\triangle PTO\) with hypotenuse \(OP = 13\) and leg \(OT = 5\):
    \[ PT = \sqrt{OP^2 - OT^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = \mathbf{12\text{ cm}} \]
  2. (b) Apply the Tangent-Secant Theorem:
    \[ PT^2 = PA \cdot PB \implies 12^2 = 8 \cdot PB \implies 144 = 8 \cdot PB \implies PB = \frac{144}{8} = 18\text{ cm} \]
    The chord length is \(AB = PB - PA = 18 - 8 = \mathbf{10\text{ cm}}\).
body.ar:
A point \(P\) is located at distance \(13\text{ cm}\) from the center \(O\) of a الدائرة with نصف القطر \(5\text{ cm}\). A خط المماس from \(P\) touches the الدائرة at point \(T\).
(a) أوجد length of the tangent segment \(PT\).
(b) A secant line through \(P\) intersects the الدائرة at points \(A\) and \(B\) such that \(PA = 8\text{ cm}\). أوجد length of chord \(AB\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Tangent Segment Length:
    Radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to tangent \(PT\), forming right المثلث \(\triangle PTO\) with hypotenuse \(OP = 13\) and leg \(OT = 5\):
    \[ PT = \sqrt{OP^2 - OT^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = \mathbf{12\text{ cm}} \]
  2. (b) Apply the Tangent-Secant مبرهنة:
    \[ PT^2 = PA \cdot PB \implies 12^2 = 8 \cdot PB \implies 144 = 8 \cdot PB \implies PB = \frac{144}{8} = 18\text{ cm} \]
    The chord length is \(AB = PB - PA = 18 - 8 = \mathbf{10\text{ cm}}\).

label.en: Worked Example 6.C — Ellipse Characteristics: Vertices, Foci, and Eccentricity
label.ar: مثال محلول 6.C — القطع الناقص Characteristics: Vertices, Foci, and Eccentricity

body.en:
An ellipse has equation \(\dfrac{(x - 2)^2}{25} + \dfrac{(y + 3)^2}{9} = 1\).
Determine: (a) coordinates of the center, (b) coordinates of the vertices, (c) coordinates of the foci, and (d) eccentricity.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Center: From \((h, k)\): \(\mathbf{(2, -3)}\).
  2. (b) Semi-axes & Vertices:
    Here \(a^2 = 25 \implies a = 5\) (horizontal major axis) and \(b^2 = 9 \implies b = 3\).
    Vertices lie \(a = 5\) units horizontally from the center:
    \[ V_1 = (2 - 5, -3) = \mathbf{(-3, -3)}, \qquad V_2 = (2 + 5, -3) = \mathbf{(7, -3)} \]
  3. (c) Foci:
    For an ellipse, \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = 25 - 9 = 16 \implies c = 4\).
    Foci lie \(c = 4\) units horizontally from the center:
    \[ F_1 = (2 - 4, -3) = \mathbf{(-2, -3)}, \qquad F_2 = (2 + 4, -3) = \mathbf{(6, -3)} \]
  4. (d) Eccentricity:
    \[ e = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{4}{5} = \mathbf{0.8} \]
body.ar:
An القطع الناقص has المعادلة \(\dfrac{(x - 2)^2}{25} + \dfrac{(y + 3)^2}{9} = 1\).
Determine: (a) الإحداثيات of the center, (b) الإحداثيات of the vertices, (c) الإحداثيات of the foci, and (d) eccentricity.

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. (a) Center: From \((h, k)\): \(\mathbf{(2, -3)}\).
  2. (b) Semi-axes & Vertices:
    Here \(a^2 = 25 \implies a = 5\) (horizontal major axis) and \(b^2 = 9 \implies b = 3\).
    Vertices lie \(a = 5\) units horizontally from the center:
    \[ V_1 = (2 - 5, -3) = \mathbf{(-3, -3)}, \qquad V_2 = (2 + 5, -3) = \mathbf{(7, -3)} \]
  3. (c) Foci:
    For an القطع الناقص, \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = 25 - 9 = 16 \implies c = 4\).
    Foci lie \(c = 4\) units horizontally from the center:
    \[ F_1 = (2 - 4, -3) = \mathbf{(-2, -3)}, \qquad F_2 = (2 + 4, -3) = \mathbf{(6, -3)} \]
  4. (d) Eccentricity:
    \[ e = \frac{c}{a} = \frac{4}{5} = \mathbf{0.8} \]

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Circles & Conic Sections (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Circles & Conic Sections (Medium Application)

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Circles & Conic Sections
label.ar: ▲ استراتيجية إدارة الوقت والتحقق في الاختبار — Circles & Conic Sections

body.en: Geometric Auxiliary-Line Strategy (Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST II — Math Level 1)): Whenever a circle problem includes a tangent line, draw the radius to the point of tangency and mark \(90^\circ\) immediately; whenever it includes a chord, drop the perpendicular bisector from the center to form a right triangle.
body.ar: Geometric Auxiliary-Line Strategy (Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST II — Math Level 1)): Whenever a الدائرة problem includes a خط المماس, draw the نصف القطر to the point of tangency and mark \(90^\circ\) immediately; whenever it includes a chord, drop the perpendicular bisector from the center to form a right المثلث.

question.en: Find the equation of the circle in standard form that passes through the three points \((0, 0)\), \((6, 0)\), and \((0, 8)\).
question.ar: أوجد equation of the circle in standard form that يمر بالنقطة the three points \((0, 0)\), \((6, 0)\), and \((0, 8)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Recognize right triangle: Points \((6, 0)\), \((0, 0)\), and \((0, 8)\) form a right triangle with right angle at \((0, 0)\). By Thales's theorem, the hypotenuse connecting \((6, 0)\) and \((0, 8)\) is the circle's diameter.

Step 2: Find center: The center \((h, k)\) is the midpoint of the diameter: \[ (h, k) = \left(\frac{6 + 0}{2}, \frac{0 + 8}{2}\right) = \mathbf{(3, 4)}. \]

Step 3: Find radius: The radius squared is the distance from center \((3, 4)\) to the origin \((0, 0)\): \[ r^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25. \]

The standard equation is \(\mathbf{(x - 3)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = 25}\).

question.en: Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) at the point \(P(3, 4)\).
question.ar: أوجد معادلة خط المماس to the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) عند النقطة \(P(3, 4)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Radius slope: The center is the origin \(O(0, 0)\). The slope of the radius connecting \((0, 0)\) and \((3, 4)\) is: \[ m_{\text{radius}} = \frac{4 - 0}{3 - 0} = \frac{4}{3}. \]

Step 2: Tangent line slope: Since the tangent is perpendicular to the radius: \[ m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{3}{4}. \]

Step 3: Point-slope equation: Using point \(P(3, 4)\): \[ y - 4 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 3) \implies 4(y - 4) = -3(x - 3) \implies 4y - 16 = -3x + 9 \implies \mathbf{3x + 4y = 25}. \]

question.en: Two chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) of a circle intersect at interior point \(M\). If \(AM = 4\text{ cm}\), \(MB = 9\text{ cm}\), and \(CM = 6\text{ cm}\), determine the length of \(MD\).
question.ar: Two chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) of a circle intersect at interior point \(M\). إذا كان \(AM = 4\text{ cm}\), \(MB = 9\text{ cm}\), and \(CM = 6\text{ cm}\), حدّد length of \(MD\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the Intersecting Chords Theorem: \[ AM \cdot MB = CM \cdot MD. \]

Step 2: Substitute given lengths: \[ 4 \times 9 = 6 \times MD \implies 36 = 6 \cdot MD. \]

Step 3: Solve for \(MD\): \[ MD = \frac{36}{6} = \mathbf{6\text{ cm}}. \]

question.en: Determine the type of conic section represented by the general quadratic equation \(4x^2 - 9y^2 + 16x + 54y - 101 = 0\), and find the coordinates of its center.
question.ar: حدّد type of conic section represented بتطبيق general quadratic equation \(4x^2 - 9y^2 + 16x + 54y - 101 = 0\), and أوجد إحداثيات its center.

solution.en:
Step 1: Identify conic type: The coefficients of \(x^2\) (\(+4\)) and \(y^2\) (\(-9\)) have opposite signs (\(A \cdot C = 4(-9) = -36 < 0\)). Therefore, the equation represents a hyperbola.

Step 2: Complete the square to locate center: \[ 4(x^2 + 4x + 4) - 9(y^2 - 6y + 9) = 101 + 4(4) - 9(9) \] \[ 4(x + 2)^2 - 9(y - 3)^2 = 101 + 16 - 81 = 36 \] Divide through by 36: \[ \frac{(x + 2)^2}{9} - \frac{(y - 3)^2}{4} = 1. \]

The center is \(\mathbf{(-2, 3)}\).
